description:
RULED by the USER s488 (2026-09-17) on Fable's recommendation (open since s486): the skip registry (`cl/skip-registry.lisp`, 103 patterns / 24 files, relabels ~198 failing rows per sweep as `ok N # skip [registry] reason`) and the `NS:` cause column of `baselines/fail-baseline.tsv` (s486a, `PCLCauses::cause_class`) both say "not supported" -- two mechanisms own one fact. The registry is RETIRED; the cause column stays. Scheduled AFTER the next tag because the headline fail count moves 649 -> ~830 (the registry rows join the fail count; the PASS count does not move) and the README/STATUS figures are refreshed at tag time (s488 ruling 3). Blocked by the TAG (an event, not a task). RECIPE (mechanical -- every registry reason already cites a not-supported.md section): 1. One sweep on a clean tree; from `.faillog` take every row the registry relabelled (the `[registry]` marker; 198 at s486b). Each becomes a `fail-baseline.tsv` row whose cause is `NS:
` copied from the registry entry's reason -- ROW BY ROW, never a bless; `tools/cause-census.pl --hygiene` clean. 2. Delete `cl/skip-registry.lisp` and its loader in `cl/pcl-test.lisp` (the `[registry]` marker + the stale detector). The s486b instruments become dead: the two `_status.tsv` columns `registry_skips`/`registry_stale`, the `(N by the registry)` TOTAL suffix + `REGISTRY-STALE:` line in `tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl`, the `REGISTRY` line in `tools/sweep-diff.pl`, the registry field in `tools/cause-census.pl` (+ its `tools/t/cause-census.t` rows), the `registry` reads in `tools/run-perl-suite.pl` and `tools/dup-census.pl` -- remove them in the same batch, or keep them reading zero if removal costs more than it saves; the batch decides and SAYS WHY. 3. The stale detector's replacement is the sweep's FIXED bucket: a migrated row that starts passing shows as FIXED in sweep-diff and leaves the baseline by edit (the standing rule). No new mechanism. 4. Docs: CLAUDE.md principle 5 ("declarative skip-registry") rewritten to the cause column; `docs/test-skip-registry.md` -> `docs/history/`; `docs/test-debugging-runbook.md`'s REGISTER branch -> "add the row with an `NS:` cause"; STATUS.md/README at the tag refresh; a DECIDED line. 5. BAR: sweep TOTAL passing UNCHANGED; `sweep-diff` 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST after the baseline edit; cause-census NS count up by EXACTLY the migrated rows; the gate green (grep Pl/t + tools/t for `skip-registry`/`registry` rows first and rewrite or delete them with the mechanism); NO companion leg needed (the companion never loads the registry, s486b). Pointers: DECIDED `## s486b` (the two-mechanisms ruling, the counting), `## s486` (the measurement: ~180-198 relabelled rows OUTSIDE the 649; 19 stale entries had accumulated -- the failure mode the retirement removes), `## s488` (this ruling). === THE TITLE -> ID TABLE (s531b member 2, 2026-11-01; Fable ruling s531 #5) === docs/not-supported.md now carries a STABLE ID above every ## / ### heading (``, read by tools/ns-ids.pl --list / --check; the grammar is docs/failure-cause-classes.md "The grammar"). Step 1 of this task writes `NS:` DIRECTLY, never a title. The titles cl/skip-registry.lisp and baselines/perl-suite-expected.tsv cite today (both files left untouched by s531b), and their ids: skip-registry title (count of reasons) -> id 'Error compatibility for invalid Perl input' (36) -> ns-invalid-perl 'Error message text and format' (14) -> ns-error-text 'Lvalue subroutines' (13; "/ arylen magic" too) -> ns-lvalue-subs 'reset() for one-match ?pattern? and named captures' (11) -> ns-reset 'DESTROY called by garbage collector' (12) -> ns-destroy-gc 'Unicode semantics differences' (8; pack 'U', utf8 flag, utf8::encode/decode) -> ns-unicode-semantics 'Unicode semantics differences' (use bytes) (7) -> ns-use-bytes 'NUL bytes (and other control characters) in identifiers' (6) -> ns-nul-identifiers 'Warnings-gated diagnostics are absent' (5) / "warning emission" (1) -> ns-warnings 'Boolean REFERENCE identity and read-only booleans (\!0)' (5) -> ns-boolean-ref-identity 'Read-only constants via \undef stash tricks' (4) -> ns-readonly-undef-stash 'Internals::* C-level introspection' (2) / "read-only scalars / Internals" (1) -> ns-internals '@_ argument aliasing' (2) -> ns-args-aliasing 'Sparse arrays (holes), element aliasing, and SV identity' (2) -> ns-sparse-arrays 'pack/unpack — pointer types (p/P)' (2) -> ns-pack-pointers 'format / write report formatting' (2) -> ns-format-write 'Writing to $a/$b inside a sort comparator' (1) -> ns-sort-ab-writes 'Computed goto (goto EXPR)' (1) -> ns-computed-goto 'A LITERAL reached through sort / reverse / grep in a foreach list is writable' -> ns-literal-writable-in-foreach 'Context propagation into string eval' (1, the comment calling it WRONG) -> ns-string-eval-context perl-suite-expected.tsv `not-supported.md §title` (files) -> id §mro — ... (all mro variants, ~50) -> ns-mro §Unicode — \p{} property classes (10) -> ns-unicode-properties §Perl 5.38 class/field/method (10) -> ns-class-syntax §Error compatibility for invalid Perl input (4) -> ns-invalid-perl §DynaLoader / XS binary extensions (3) -> ns-xs §`given`/`when` / smart match (3) -> ns-given-when §symbol-table hashes (... *Foo:: = *Bar::, isarev) (6) -> ns-live-stash-hashes §Readouts of perl's own internals (2) -> ns-perl-internals-readouts §Error message text and format / §error-text (3) -> ns-error-text §DESTROY called by garbage collector (2) -> ns-destroy-gc §Unicode semantics differences (2) -> ns-unicode-semantics §use bytes / §use vN default warnings / §Control-character glob names (1) -> ns-use-bytes, ns-use-vn-warnings, ns-control-char-globs §Integers are unbounded (1) -> ns-integers-unbounded §Regex script-run assertions (1) -> ns-regex-script-run §Regex extended character classes (1) -> ns-regex-extended-class §regex-code-blocks (2) -> ns-regex-code-blocks §defer { … } (1) -> ns-defer §Lexical compile-time hints (1) -> ns-compile-hints §pathological-nesting (1) -> ns-nesting-depth §__SUB__ (1) -> ns-current-sub §Internals::* (1) -> ns-internals §format / write report formatting (1) -> ns-format-write "Interned boolean constants" (1) -- NO section by that title; the nearest is ns-boolean-ref-identity (confirm when the row moves) The full id list: `tools/ns-ids.pl --list` (128 ids; four RETIRED: ns-bare-if-empty, ns-refaliasing, ns-triple-deref, ns-pow-exact-integer). === THE VALIDATOR FLIPS THE COMPANION TO GATE IN THIS BATCH (s531b, Fable ruling s531 #8) === Pl/t/verdict-register-01.t (s531b) checks every cause's KEY (docs/failure-cause-classes.md "The KEY is checked"). It is the GATE for the CPAN board today and a REPORT (counts via note, never a failing row) for baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv, fail-baseline.tsv and row-shortfall.tsv. When THIS task's batch migrates those rows (`NS:` written directly, from the title -> id table above), it also moves those three populations from REPORT to GATE in the validator (the `for my $p (...)` REPORT loop becomes three more `scan` + `is` blocks like the board's). The REPORT at s531b (the tree's store; the live store may differ) -- the queue that batch inherits: companion: 10,141 rows -- 5,855 not in the grammar (legacy NS titles + task-first ruling cells), 269 rows keyed on a CLOSED task (16 tasks: #376 62, #1719 50, #155 39, #2380 29, #1870 28, #3492 16, #1709 15, #2372 9, #1236 6, #1587 6, ...), 2 on a MISSING task (#1722), 43 on an id-less task file (#407 40, #408 3 -- the three store files with no `id` field, 407-409) sweep (fail-baseline.tsv): 459 rows -- 289 not in the grammar, 19 keyed on a closed task (#1028 6, #449 3, #972 3, #1021 2, #1024 2, #2101 2, #1456 1), 1 on an id-less file (#408) shortfall (row-shortfall.tsv): 217 rows -- 119 not in the grammar, 4 keyed on a closed task (#376, #1590, #1870, #2380) Each closed-key row needs a one-file companion run before it is re-caused (CLOSE-WITH-ROWS, ruling 3). The tool: tools/migrate-causes.pl's shape (it handles the board's format; that batch adds the other three formats or a sibling).
